title: TEE audit rule
description: One detectable failure mode. Every rule must cite the source that justifies it.

id.description: BT-T## threat rules, BT-CFG## build/deploy config, BT-DS## dstack-specific, BT-LYR## layer scoring.

source.description: REQUIRED. The handbook section this rule is derived from. A rule with no source is not a rule.

source_secondary.description: Primary sources for rules that are independently defensible (RFCs, vendor docs, CVEs). Present on every rule we would still ship if the handbook did not exist.

threat.description: Handbook 'Dumb Ways to Get Rekt' threat number, where the rule maps to one.

layer_required.description: Lowest handbook security layer (0-6) that requires this rule to pass. Drives the scorecard: failing a rule caps the protocol below this layer.

detection.description: deterministic = parse/AST/grep, no model call. semantic = requires judgment. hybrid = deterministic prefilter, semantic adjudication.

detector.description: Implementing detector id, e.g. semgrep:tee/timing-oracle-compare, core:eif-secret-scan, agent:trust-boundary.

rationale.description: Why this is exploitable. Mechanism, not restatement of the title.

attack.description: Documented real-world exploitation, where the handbook or public record names one.

false_positives.description: REQUIRED. When this rule is wrong. A rule whose author cannot name its failure mode has not been thought through, and an unreviewed rule inflates the FP rate the benchmark exists to measure.

confidence.description: Expected precision of the detector, set before benchmarking and corrected by it. Divergence between this and the measured number is itself a result.

status.description: draft = catalogued only. implemented = detector exists and passes fixtures. benchmarked = precision/recall measured on the mutation corpus.
